questions.question: 1. How is a linear search performed?

answers.a: An element is copied into another array until the required element is found
answers.b: The array is broken into smaller subarrays and the elements are searched recursively
answers.c: The array is traversed sequentially from one end until the required element is found or the array ends
answers.d: The array is sorted first and then only the middle element is checked

explanations.a: Incorrect. Linear search does not require creating another array.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Dividing the array into smaller subarrays is not the defining procedure of linear search.
explanations.c: Correct. Linear search checks the elements sequentially, usually from the first element toward the last, until the target is found or no elements remain.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Linear search does not require sorting the array or checking only its middle element.

questions.question: 2. In the worst case, what is the time complexity of linear search on an array of size $N$?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Linear search does not repeatedly reduce the search space by a constant factor.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The search may need to inspect many elements before terminating.
explanations.c: Correct. In the worst case, all $N$ elements may need to be checked, giving $O(N)$ time.
explanations.d: Incorrect. A single sequential traversal does not require $O(N \log N)$ operations.

questions.question: 3. In the best case, what is the time complexity of linear search?

explanations.a: Correct. If the required element is the first element examined, only one comparison is required, giving $O(1)$ time.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The best case requires only a constant number of operations.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Linear search does not halve the search space in the best case.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Checking all $N$ elements corresponds to the worst case rather than the best case.

questions.question: 4. How is linear search disadvantageous compared with search methods that exploit additional structure such as sorted order?

answers.a: It may require more comparisons to find an element
answers.b: It always requires additional memory proportional to the array size
answers.c: It is difficult to implement because it requires recursion
answers.d: It cannot be used on an unsorted array

explanations.a: Correct. Linear search may need to inspect many elements, whereas some algorithms can use additional structure to reduce the number of comparisons.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A standard linear search can be performed using constant auxiliary space.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Linear search can be implemented simply with an iterative loop and a comparison.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Linear search is particularly useful when the array is unsorted.

questions.question: 5. For an ordered linear search, $O(N)$ is the worst-case time complexity. An ordered linear search is a linear search on an array that is already sorted.

explanations.a: Correct. Even though a sorted array can allow the search to terminate early in some cases, the worst case can still require examining all $N$ elements.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Sorting can improve some cases of linear search, but it does not eliminate the possibility of a linear worst case.

questions.question: 6. What is the best-case number of comparisons for a linear search when the target is the first element of the array?

explanations.a: Correct. The first comparison finds the target immediately.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Linear search does not use logarithmic reduction of the search range.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Checking all $N$ elements is unnecessary when the first element matches.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The search stops at the first element and does not examine the remaining elements.

questions.question: 7. Consider the array [7, 14, 3, 25, 10]. If linear search is used to find 25 from left to right, how many elements are examined?

explanations.a: Incorrect. The first two examined values are 7 and 14, neither of which is 25.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The first three values are 7, 14, and 3, so 25 has not yet been found.
explanations.c: Correct. The search checks 7, 14, 3, and then 25, so four elements are examined.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The search stops when 25 is found and does not need to examine 10.

questions.question: 8. Which statement about linear search on an unsorted array is correct?

answers.a: The array must be sorted before linear search
answers.b: Linear search can be used without sorting the array
answers.d: Linear search can inspect only the middle element

explanations.a: Incorrect. Linear search does not depend on the elements being ordered.
explanations.b: Correct. Linear search can examine the elements sequentially regardless of their ordering.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Although its best case is $O(1)$, its worst case is $O(N)$.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Linear search may inspect many positions rather than only the middle.

questions.question: 9. Suppose an unsorted array contains $N$ elements and the target is not present. What is the number of elements that a standard linear search may need to examine?

explanations.a: Incorrect. If the target is absent, the search cannot normally stop after checking only one element.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Linear search does not have a logarithmic worst-case bound.
explanations.c: Correct. When the target is absent, every one of the $N$ elements may need to be examined.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The final element also needs to be checked before the search can conclude that the target is absent.
